Akhil vs Biju N.Alias on 7 October, 2025

This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the claim petitioner in O.P. (MV) No.949/2016 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Muvattupuzha (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 16/07/2020.
The respondents herein are the respondents in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 18/08/2016 at about 08:15 p.m., while he was riding motorcycle bearing registration no.KL-39-J-8235 through Thiruvaniyoor- Maneed road,
autorickshaw bearing registration no.KL-17-H-2476 driven by the 1st respondent in a rash and negligent manner 2025:KER:74221 knocked him down, as a result of which he sustained grievous injuries.
3. The first respondent-owner cum driver of the offending autorickshaw remained ex-parte.
4. The second respondent-insurer filed written statement admitting the policy but denying negligence on the part of the first respondent.
The vehicle had no valid fitness certificate.
It was also contended that the claim petitioner had no driving license at the time of the accident.
The averments in the petition regarding age, occupation and income of the claim petitioner were disputed.
The compensation claimed under various heads was contended to be exorbitant.
5. Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts.A1 to A15 And Ext.C1 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
Ext.B1 was marked on the side of the respondents.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found 2025:KER:74221 negligence on the part of the first respondent-owner cum driver of the offending autorickshaw resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 5,21,500/- together with interest @ 7% per annum from the date of the petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.
7.
The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.

8. Heard both sides.
9. The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged by the claim petitioner- Notional income
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that the latter, a fitter was earning 20,000/- per month.
However, the Tribunal fixed the notional income at 8,000/-, which is quite low and hence the same needs to be appropriately 2025:KER:74221 enhanced.

Per contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the second respondent-insurer that the amount that is fixed is quite reasonable and that if at all the Court is inclined to enhance the same, it may be as per the dictum in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236.
9.1.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the dictum in Ramachandrappa (Supra) the income of a coolie in the year 2016 is liable to be fixed at 10,500/- per month.
In the case on hand, the fact that he is a fitter is not seen disputed and therefore, in the facts and circumstances, an amount of 12,000/- per month would be just and reasonable.
Loss of earnings 10.

The materials on record show that the claim petitioner sustained the following injuries- "
1. Brachial plexus injury right hand.
2025:KER:74221
2 . Fracture right wrist.

3. Fracture proximal phalanx of right little finger. "
He was hospitalized for a period of 21 days in five different spells.

In all probability,
he might have been unable to work for a period of 8 months.

Hence, he can be awarded compensation for loss of earnings for a period of 8 months, that is,
12,000/- x 8 = 96,000/-.
Loss of amenities
11. The relevant portion of Ext.A8 discharge summary reads thus- " Alleged history of RTA (bike vs auto) at around 8:00 p.m. on 18/08/2016 at Maneed.
No history of loss of consiousness, vomiting or seizures.
Following the trauma the patient has loss of sensation and inability to move his right upper limb.
Patient ambulant.

3
Consious and alert.
Vitals stable.
GCS - E4M6V5, PEARL Moving the left UL and both LL Loss of sensation over the right UL ............................."
(Emphasis supplied)
11.1. In the light of Ext.A8, I find that an amount of 1,00,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
Loss of marriage prospectus 12.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that due to the disability caused, a reasonable amount ought to have been awarded by the Tribunal.
However, no amount has been awarded and hence interference into the same is called for.

12.1. In the light of the disability caused, which is loss of sensation and inability to move his right upper limb and as the claim petitioner at the time of the accident was only 23 years, I find that an amount of 50,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

In the result, the appeal is allowed by enhancing the compensation by a further amount of 3,03,542/- (total compensation = 8,25,042/- that is, 5,21,500/-
granted by the Tribunal + 3,03,542/- granted in appeal) with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition till date of realization and proportionate costs.
The second respondent/ insurer is directed to deposit the aforesaid amount before the Tribunal within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment.
On deposit of the amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the amount to the claim petitioner at the earliest in accordance with law after making deductions, if any.
The liberty granted by the Tribunal to the second respondent-insurer to recover the amount from the first respondent-owner cum driver is confirmed.
Interlocutory applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.
